core.title: Place every source file beneath its plan-declared feature directory
core.given: The plan under the plan root models at least one product capability, feature or DESIRED OUTCOME, and source files exist beneath the source root (the profile's configured source root), excluding the stack's vendored and generated trees.
core.when: Any source file beneath the source root is checked, whatever its language. This covers new, moved and existing unchanged files.
core.then: Each such file lives beneath the profile's feature directory for its product capability and feature, for a feature the plan declares.
prefer: Fix a finding by moving the file beneath its feature's directory and adding the component URN binding.
Make the product capability and feature segments of the file's component URN match the feature directory the file lives in.
avoid: Source files beneath the source root placed outside any feature directory.
Placing source under a feature directory the plan does not declare.

Leaving an in-scope source file without a well-formed component URN binding (product capability, feature, name, side, layer role). The same check fails on this, so treat it as required alongside placement. Its obligation is proposed as a separate split rule (source URN header).
unless: Vendored and generated trees are never scanned.
core.why: Source is traced to its owning feature by its URN and found by its path. If either is missing, nobody can show that the feature has an implementation.
evidence: The stack's topology check reports no finding for any file beneath the source root. Every file sits under the feature directory of a plan-declared feature and has a well-formed component URN binding.
verification: Strict disposition: the rule fails on every finding. There is no advisory mode.

Precondition: the rule is active only when the plan models at least one product capability, feature or DESIRED OUTCOME. It then checks every source file beneath the source root, not only changed files, with no language filter.
The stack-wide excluded (vendored and generated) trees are skipped and are never findings.
Files outside the source root are not covered by this check.

The same check also reports a missing or malformed component URN binding on any in-scope file (including when the plan models only DESIRED OUTCOMES); that obligation belongs to the proposed split rule for the source URN header.

values: source file beneath the source root (any language; new, moved or unchanged; excluded trees skipped)
plan models >=1 product capability, feature or DESIRED OUTCOME

fires: The plan models at least one product capability, feature or DESIRED OUTCOME, and any source file beneath the source root (new, moved or existing and unchanged) sits outside a feature directory.
The plan models at least one product capability, feature or DESIRED OUTCOME, and a source file beneath the source root sits under a feature directory the plan does not declare.

The plan models at least one product capability, feature or DESIRED OUTCOME (including a plan that models only DESIRED OUTCOMES), and an in-scope source file has a missing or malformed component URN binding. The same check reports this; the obligation belongs to the proposed split rule for the source URN header.
doesNotFire: Files in vendored or generated trees.
The plan does not yet model any product capability, feature or DESIRED OUTCOME.

neutralityNotes: Wagon, feature and WMBT are ATDD plan concepts, not stack concepts, so they stay in the core. The URN-header obligation is mirrored in avoid[2], fires[2], evidence[0] and verification as in bun.json, pending the proposed split rule (legacy id atdd-bun.topology.source-urn-header); the core refers to it generically. The path_glob activation fact has no core fact type and is expressed through file_kind plus roots.source. Strict disposition comes from the shared policy node policy.strict-disposition.
